Answers.content:
The assumption that each desk has 10 red markers is given directly in the problem statement. Specifically, it is mentioned that "each desk has 10 red markers." This information is used to calculate the total number of red markers for a given number of desks.

For 3 desks, the calculation would be:
\[ \text{Total red markers} = \text{Number of desks} \times \text{Red markers per desk} \]
\[ \text{Total red markers} = 3 \times 10 = 30 \]

Thus, there are 30 red markers on 3 desks.
